name: MATP (cream / pearl)
summary: SLC45A2 on chromosome 21, formerly called MATP: the locus of cream and pearl. It dilutes the pigment the base colour produces and makes no colour of its own. Cream (Cr, c.457G>A) is incompletely dominant: one copy turns red to gold and barely touches black, giving palomino on a chestnut, buckskin on a bay and smoky black on a black; two copies dilute both pigments strongly, giving cremello, perlino or smoky cream with pink skin and blue eyes. Pearl (Prl, c.985G>A) is recessive: one copy shows nothing, and two dilute both red and black. Cream with pearl gives a pseudo-double cream that looks like a double cream and is not one. Cream is described as common in Quarter Horses, Paint Horses, the American Cream Draft, Icelandic Horses, Welsh ponies and many gaited breeds, without published figures. Pearl is found in Andalusians, Lusitanos, Quarter Horses and Paint Horses, where it was once called the Barlink factor. Two further alleles are proposed. Snowdrop (c.305G>A on the EquCab2.0 transcript, the same change as c.449G>A on the EquCab3.0 one; g.31688649G>A on chromosome 21, EquCab3.0) is a published candidate, recessive, known from one Gypsy Cob family: one homozygous mare that looked cremello and several relatives with one copy and no visible dilution. No horse with snowdrop beside cream or pearl has been reported, and laboratories that test for it say its effect beside other SLC45A2 variants is unknown. Sunshine (c.568G>A, p.Gly190Arg) is disputed: it was proposed in 2019 from about 130 phenotyped horses, as a pearl-like dilution in horses that also carried another dilution, with no horse found with two copies; a 2024 sequencing study of 605 horses from 48 breeds then found 146 horses with one copy and 390 with two, and the variant was the commoner allele in all 12 breed groups, above 0.86 in Arabians, Belgians, Morgans, Thoroughbreds and Quarter Horses, mostly in horses with no dilution. It is not rare; whether it dilutes at all is unresolved. With no exact figure per breed, it is left out of the frequency tables. No effect on build, performance or health is established.

alleles.name: Snowdrop (C^sno; c.305G>A, p.Arg102Gln, also written c.449G>A, p.Arg150Gln) - candidate

phenotypes.name: Pearl carrier
phenotypes.description: One pearl copy. No visible effect on any base colour; the horse passes the copy to half its foals.

phenotypes.name: Snowdrop carrier
phenotypes.description: One snowdrop copy. Reported to have no visible effect: relatives of the first snowdrop horse that carried one copy looked undiluted.

phenotypes.name: Single cream
phenotypes.description: One cream copy. Red pigment is diluted to yellow or gold and black is barely touched: palomino on a chestnut, buckskin on a bay with its black points kept, and smoky black on a black, which can be hard or impossible to tell from black by eye.

phenotypes.name: Pearl
phenotypes.description: Two pearl copies. Both red and black pigment are diluted, in the coat, mane, tail and skin; on a chestnut the result is a pale, even apricot body, mane and tail over pale skin.

phenotypes.name: Pseudo-double cream
phenotypes.description: One cream copy and one pearl copy. A pale coat, pale skin and often blue or green eyes: it looks like a double cream but carries one cream allele, not two, and breeds accordingly.

phenotypes.name: Snowdrop
phenotypes.description: Two snowdrop copies. In the one horse known, a Gypsy Cob mare, both red and black pigment were diluted to a very pale coat like a double cream. No unrelated horse with two copies is reported.

phenotypes.name: Pair with sunshine (disputed)
phenotypes.description: A pair that includes the sunshine variant. It was proposed as a recessive dilution after being found in a horse that looked like a double cream and had only one cream allele. Later work found the variant at very high frequency in many breeds, mostly in horses with no dilution, so whether it reduces pigment at all is unresolved. No outcome is given.

phenotypes.name: Snowdrop with cream or pearl (not documented)
phenotypes.description: Snowdrop beside cream or pearl. No tested horse with either pair is reported - not in the paper that found snowdrop, nor by the laboratories that test for it, one of which says the effect is still unknown. A dilution is plausible, since cream with pearl dilutes, but unobserved, so no outcome is given.

phenotypes.name: Double cream
phenotypes.description: Two cream copies. Both red and black pigment are strongly diluted: cremello on a chestnut, perlino on a bay, smoky cream on a black, with pink skin and blue eyes. Black-based double creams may keep a little more pigment than chestnut-based ones.

frequencies.population: Lusitano (allele frequencies Cr 0.42 and prl 0.064, relatedness-filtered, Avila et al. 2022; genotype shares worked out from them assuming random mating; horses tested at a laboratory, not a random sample; sunshine not counted)
